metadata.body:
# PoroTomo Induced-Seismicity Agent

Blueprint for clio-agent. The numeric work lives in plain scripts in this
repository so it can run on PBS compute nodes without an LLM:

- `agent/manifest.py`: list the DASV records on `s3://nrel-pds-porotomo/` and sample them.
- `agent/detect.py`: per-record detector (common-mode removal, 10-150 Hz band-pass, median STA/LTA).
- `agent/pbs/submit.sh`: submit the distributed detection plus aggregation job to Aurora.
- `agent/hazard.py`: anomaly z-scores, event catalogue, pumping volumes, seismogenic index, probabilities.

The experts orchestrate those scripts, inspect files, and explain results. They
never make up numbers. Every figure they report comes from `summary.json` or a
tool result.

Install by linking this directory into `~/.config/clio-agent/agent-blueprints/`.

agent_blueprint.name: PoroTomo Induced-Seismicity Agent

session.title: porotomo-induced-seismicity: Report the headline results of the agent

answer:
Headline results of the completed agent run (read-only report; nothing was executed, submitted, or modified — no hazard.py, no PBS jobs).

RUN
- Run directory: /home/hyoklee/poro/agent/results/run_20261115T155359Z_s20 (run id run_20261115T155359Z_s20; summary.json generated 2026-11-15T16:02:33+00:00)
- PBS job 9092130.aurora-pbs (2 nodes x 24 ranks = 48 ranks); detection started 2026-11-15T15:57:45Z, hazard finished 2026-11-15T16:00:56Z
- Source of all numbers: summary.json in that directory (cross-checked against detect.log, anomalies.csv, events.csv, hazard_rerun.log, interpretation.md)

RECORDS ANALYSED
- 759 DAS/HDF5 records analysed (manifest: 15,164 total records, selected 759 at stride 20 = every 20th record, i.e. one 30-s record per 10 min; sampled fraction of total time ≈ 0.0331, i.e. ~3.3%). Window: first record 2016-03-18T02:09:17Z, last 2016-03-26T00:59:44Z. All 759 records status "ok" (6 initial curl SSL_read EOF failures were retried successfully via detect_retry_login.jsonl).

ANOMALIES AND DAS DETECTIONS
- Anomalous records: 57 (z_threshold = 5.0; top anomaly 2016-03-23T20:50:17Z, zmax = 30.92, driver max_sta_lta)
- DAS detections (das_events): 62 events across 53 records; scaled to full time: n_scaled_to_full_time = 1870.77; relative b (Aki MLE on DAS magnitudes) = 0.9849, mc_relative = -0.8492, n_above_mc = 34

SEISMOGENIC INDEX Sigma (log10 seismicity-rate density, Shapiro et al. 2021 Eq. 5 Poisson model P = 1 - exp(-V * 10^(Sigma - b*M)))
- Catalogue-conditioned (LBNL/NCEDC March 2016, GDR 859, n=5 events, mc=-0.48, mag_max=0.07): b=1.0 -> Sigma = -5.4489; b=0.73 -> Sigma = -5.3193; b=0.65 -> Sigma = -5.2809
- DAS-based: Sigma = -2.6983 with b_used = 0.9849 (b_source: DAS relative-magnitude Aki MLE)

P(Mw >= 5.5) PER YEAR, PER b SCENARIO — CALIBRATED (hazard_catalog_based, "p_per_year_at_observed_rate", LBNL catalogue)
- b = 1.0: 0.00011982478978644906 /yr (~1.20e-04; p over observed volume = 5.24e-06)
- b = 0.73: 0.004921548824626587 /yr (~4.92e-03; p over observed volume = 2.16e-04)
- b = 0.65: 0.014735103451029574 /yr (~1.47e-02; p over observed volume = 6.48e-04)

DAS-BASED UPPER BOUND — UNCALIBRATED (hazard_das_upper_bound, b = 0.9849)
- P(Mw >= 5.5) = 0.07842182774171746 /yr (~7.84e-02; p over observed volume = 2.41e-03)
- Derivation: treats EVERY DAS detection (62 detections, scaled to 1870.77 over full time) as an event at/above the catalogue minimum magnitude mc=-0.48, so it over-counts; it is an upper bound only, with uncalibrated DAS-derived magnitudes.

WHICH IS CALIBRATED
- CALIBRATED: the catalogue-based numbers (hazard_catalog_based) — LBNL/NCEDC March 2016 local catalogue (only 5 events, calibrated ML), assuming each b value and the Shapiro et al. (2021) Eq. 5 model at the observed rate/volume. Use these for any decision.
- UPPER BOUND, NOT CALIBRATED: the DAS-based 7.84e-02/yr — over-counts detections as catalogued-magnitude events and extrapolates from limited DAS magnitudes.

ASSUMPTIONS / CAVEATS (from summary.json and interpretation.md)
- Only ~3.3% of total time sampled (stride 20); rare events could be missed; 8-day DAS window within a 16-day pumping period.
- Catalogue probabilities rest on a very small local catalogue (5 events) and the assumed b values; Sigma choice dominates the probability.
- Site Sigma (-5.45 to -5.28) is far below the Sigma needed for a 1% chance of Mw>=5.5 over the observed volume (b=1.0: -2.166; b=0.73: -3.651; b=0.65: -4.091).
- Pohang reference block: sigma_range [-2.0, -1.0], b in [0.65, 0.73], mainshock Mw 5.5 (2017-11-15), reported worst-case probabilities 0.15-0.17; v_fig3c = 5850 m3; total injected 12,800 m3.
- Pumping context (GDR 917): 2016-03-11 to 2016-03-27, net injected -40,485 m3 (extraction exceeded injection); weakly negative Spearman correlations between hourly events and net injection (-0.17) — no causality claimed.
- Reviewer note in interpretation.md flags three errors in the raw report text (stride meaning; catalogue-based — not DAS — is the calibrated estimate; direction of the Sigma-vs-1% statement); the values above follow the corrected reading.

Bottom line: at Brady Hot Springs in this March 2016 DAS window, the calibrated catalogue-based P(Mw>=5.5) is 1.2e-04 to 1.5e-02 per year depending on b (1.0 -> 0.65), while the DAS-only figure of 7.8e-02 per year is an uncalibrated upper bound.
